_comment: Baselines for bench/kotlin-import-target/measure.mjs --check. `fingerprint` is a sha256 over every `fromFile | targetRaw -> result` triple the correctness corpus resolves, in BOTH file-set iteration orders; it is a CORRECTNESS gate, so drift means Kotlin import resolution started returning a different file set and IMPORTS/CALLS edges moved in every Kotlin repository. Explain it, never re-baseline to make CI green. `cases` is asserted alongside it because a shrunken corpus produces a perfectly valid fingerprint over a smaller surface — the two fields must be re-baselined together and deliberately. `scaling_budget` is a timing gate and carries deliberate headroom for shared CI runners.
_provenance: This fingerprint is the value the PRE-INDEX implementation produced. It was not read off the new code: the same corpus was run against `git show <pre-index>:gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/kotlin/import-target.ts` — the four-tier per-import scan — and against the index that replaced it. Both printed 5ad605c179081505705ff7698a09dbdbdc4831080af6d9fdec5499cc6bce28ee over 20074 cases, 11612 of them non-null. That is what makes the index change a performance change rather than a behaviour change, and it is reproducible: swap the module specifier at the top of measure.mjs for the old file and re-run. The corpus deliberately includes the shapes where the two could have diverged — repeated directory names whose FIRST occurrence is not the parent (`data/src/main/kotlin/com/example/data/Repo.kt` is NOT a child of `data`, because the old scan tested startsWith and then used indexOf), doubly nested same-name directories, an exact match appearing after a suffix match in iteration order, `.kt`/`.kts` stem collisions, backslash paths, repo-root files, wildcard `.*` targets landing on the single-file tier rather than fanning out, and non-Kotlin noise.
_scaling_note: (t_large/t_small)/(1600/400). ~1.0 is linear. OBSERVED BAND: 0.98-1.00 over three unloaded runs on a 12-core dev box, small arm ~8 ms. IMPORTS_PER_FILE is sized so the small arm lands in the tens of ms rather than the ~2 ms the first revision measured, where timer granularity and JIT warm-up — not scaling — set the number; bench/cpp-qualified-ns documents the same artifact. TRIAGE: a scaling failure is a TIMING signal — RE-RUN IT on an idle machine before investigating; runner contention dominates. The fingerprint arm is the opposite: deterministic, a re-run never changes it, and it must never be wished away. FLOOR CHECK: the pre-index implementation — i.e. exactly the regression this gate exists to catch — measures 2207.8 ms small, 33003.5 ms large, ratio 3.737 on this same corpus, against 8.0 ms / 31.7 ms and 0.99 for the index. The budget of 1.6 therefore separates the two by a wide margin in both directions. Read the absolute times as an order of magnitude only (~276x small, ~1041x large): the floor arm was run once cold, because best-of-seven against the quadratic implementation costs ~5 minutes of wall time, while the index arm is the usual best-of-seven after two warmups. The RATIOS are the comparable pair — each is internally consistent, both arms of each implementation measured the same way.
